prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: transparent coral triangle cutout, single targeted camera/geometry correction.
Input image 1 is the APPROVED original scene and the binding object identity and camera reference. Input image 2 is a draft cutout to correct. Use the BACK-RIGHT coral triangular prism in input 1 as the exact model.

Correct only the draft cutout's geometry/view: its LEFT thickness plane is currently much too broad and reads like a deep wedge. In the approved object the visible dark left thickness is NARROW, around 8 to 12 percent of total horizontal bounding-box width at the base, while almost all of the visible object is the large coral triangular FRONT face. Match that original thin triangular wooden tile, almost front-facing, in the same very mild 3/4 angle. At intended native composition size the approved back-right piece spans roughly 120 pixels wide by 114 pixels tall. Keep a slightly backward-sloping bottom line rising to the right as in the original. The top point, front-face right corner and front-face left corner form the same broad near-equilateral coral triangle. Do not turn it into a pyramid or deep prism.
Preserve original warm salmon/coral painted-wood material, fine grain and subtle bevel, with darker narrow left thickness and sunny top/right edges. No creative redesign and no stronger material roughness.

Return ONE complete corrected piece alone on true transparent alpha in a square canvas with about 10 percent transparent margins. Keep all three corners and tip fully inside frame. No floor, external cast shadow, rail, other objects, pedestal, text, checkerboard, borders, labels, UI or colored background. Intrinsic object shading only; the build supplies contact shadow. The background must be genuinely transparent.
